answer: J. R. R. Tolkien wrote The Hobbit. He was an English author and Oxford professor. The book's full title is The Hobbit, or There and Back Again, and George Allen & Unwin first published it as a children's fantasy novel on 21 September 1937 [1]. Tolkien later said the idea came to him while he was marking exam papers, when he wrote down the line "In a hole in the ground there lived a hobbit" [1]. The Hobbit was the forerunner to his much larger work, The Lord of the Rings, which came out in 1954–55 [1].
